title: Outcome after Akin osteotomy with suture refixation vs. nitinol staples.
summary:
Various methods are available for performing the Akin osteotomy. Sutures can be used to close the bone gap after a wedge has been removed to correct malposition, or staples can be used.
The staples used in this study have been in use since August 2018.
The aim is to compare the results for fixation with thread and staples, as there is not yet such comprehensive scientific data for staples due to their shorter duration of use.
Whenever implants are used, discomfort may be caused by these implants. However, the advantage of the staples may also be that they allow greater compression of the bone gap.
The study will compare the osseous regrowth of the two methods in the X-ray control twelve weeks after surgery.
In addition, the frequency in the occurrence of the gegebebenen possible complaints related to the brace after 6 months, as well as the revision rate and survival time of the implant (including a comparison in terms of risk factors and pre-existing conditions) will be collected and compared.
Patients will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups (suture or staple) immediately before hallux valgus surgery. On the day of admission, as well as at the 12-week and 6-month follow-up visits, patients are asked to complete questionnaires (EFAS and FAOS). In accordance with orthopedic routine, X-ray examinations also take place at these time points.

interventions.name:
In patients undergoing surgical correction of hallux valgus deformity, Akin osteotomy is performed using NiTinol staples.
Patients are clinically examined, x-rayed, and scores are collected (VAS for pain, EFAS, FAOS) both before surgery and at follow-up visits (6 weeks, 12 weeks, and 6 months).

In patients undergoing surgical correction of hallux valgus deformity, Akin osteotomy is performed using sutures.
Patients are clinically examined, x-rayed, and scores are collected (VAS for pain, EFAS, FAOS) both before surgery and at follow-up visits (6 weeks, 12 weeks, and 6 months).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with indication for Akin osteotomy
- Age 18-80 years
Exclusion criteria:
- Florid infection
- Fractures that occurred less than 6 months ago
- Arthrodesis or osteotomy proximal to the Lisfranc joint row 
- Wheelchair requirement
